This edition · 28–29 October · 45 stories

Comebacks

Old forms, new terms

Comebacks run through this edition. Versace is returning Atelier Versace to the couture schedule in January 2027, part of a wider couture boom that Vogue traces through Hermès’s debut the same month. PlayStation revives the translucent hardware of the late 1990s with its Prism Collection, Bottega Veneta breaks five years of Instagram silence, and Creative Bloq finds Apple trading millennial minimalism for Gen Z playfulness. Not every revival lasts: the Guardian reports that mid-century modern has passed its peak. Koto’s identity for a newly pedestrianised Oxford Street leads, pitching a much-maligned street as one ‘for everyone’. Elsewhere, AI is treated less as a threat than a mirror – from The Drum’s warning that it is amplifying branding’s myths to UX Collective’s argument that the field’s crisis was 20 years in the making. And home is being rethought at every scale, from refugee cities to Mars.

Lead story · Rebrands & New Identity

Oxford Street gets its first brand identity as it enters a new eraKU

Creative Review · 29 Oct · all images: Koto

Oxford Street has a new brand identity, created by Koto to accompany the pedestrianisation of a stretch of the central London thoroughfare. Titled For Everyone, it is intended to reposition one of Britain’s most recognisable – and much-maligned – streets as a destination for culture, leisure and public life, as well as retail.

Why it matters: the identity has to sell what pedestrianisation changes – a street for spending time rather than passing through – and Creative Review is clear that the public space and the mix of businesses, not branding alone, will decide whether it works.

“We set out to build an identity around what has always made it extraordinary: its ability to constantly change.”
James Greenfield, founder and CEO, Koto
“It’s a place of firsts, of celebration, of everyday encounters.”
Sam Howard, creative director, Koto
